sources: Price of lighting in the United Kingdom, constant 2000 British pounds per million lumen-hours, 1301–2006: Fouquet & Pearson (2006), 'Seven Centuries of Energy Services: The Price and Use of Light in the United Kingdom (1300-2000)', The Energy Journal 27(1); Fouquet & Pearson (2012); via Our World in Data (owid-datasets 'Price for Light – Fouquet'). 1301: 33,043; 1500: 14,472; 1800: 9,540; 1850: 2,525; 1900: 236; 1950: 14.7; 2006: 2.89 -> 33,043 / 2.89 = about 11,400x.
Weighted average over lighting sources (candles, oil, gas, kerosene, electricity), inflation-adjusted with Bank of England long-run price indices.
